summary: This partial P7/R03 checkpoint contains 210 declarations, preserving all 192 incoming node objects and the full general Noetherian-local finite-module Hilbert–Samuel key. Eighteen new declarations compare the actual equation-jet image with successive powers of the curve variable ideal, then identify the homogeneous polynomial quotient with the actual degree piece. Fifteen named boundary tests cover zero/unit equations, no variables, nilpotent coefficients and the characteristic-two nonreduced equation. Degreewise principal kernels retain exact-order and no-zero-divisors hypotheses. Multiplicative full graded assembly, dimension, general multiplicity and all inherited stage/source obligations remain open.

declarations.provides: For any commutative Noetherian ring R and finite R-module M, a RelSeries of actual submodules from bottom to top whose successive quotients are R/p. No local, complete, Dedekind, finite-length or freeness assumption is present.

declarations.provides: An induction principle for a property of finite R-modules in a fixed module universe: prove the subsingleton case, every module linearly equivalent to R/p, and preservation across a short exact sequence specified by an injective first map, surjective second map and Function.Exact. nodes.title: Nilpotent uniformizer in a finite algebra
nodes.statement: Let O be a discrete valuation ring, pi an irreducible element of O, and A a commutative O-algebra finite as an O-module. If the image of pi is nilpotent in A, then A is Artinian. Neither localness or reducedness of A nor finiteness of the residue field of O is assumed.
hypotheses: All scalar actions come from the given unital O-algebra structure.
The zero algebra is allowed; a nilpotence witness of exponent zero forces this case.
proofSteps: Choose n with pi_A^n=0. The algebra map factors through O/(pi^n), since every multiple of pi^n maps to zero. The same finite O-generators generate A over that quotient: lift each quotient coefficient to O. Construct the quotient scalar action, not a new coefficient-ring type.

The uniformizer identity identifies (pi^n) with m_O^n. The pinned length formula gives O-module length n for this quotient; length_ne_top_iff and the finite-length equivalence make it Artinian as an O-module. Apply the pinned isArtinian_of_tower to the quotient scalar tower to make it an Artinian ring. Equivalently its ideals are O-submodules. This is scalar restriction, not finite cardinality.
Apply IsArtinianRing.of_finite to A over O/(pi^n). This includes n=0 by the zero-ring branch.
acceptance: For A=O/(pi^n)[t]/(t^2), the hypothesis holds and the conclusion is dimension at most zero, despite nonzero nilpotents.
For A=O[t]/(pi*t,t^2), pi is not nilpotent; the lemma must not infer Artinianness merely from pi-torsion.
The proof still applies when the residue field of O is infinite; it uses length, not the number of elements.

nodes.title: Coefficient injection at a generic prime
nodes.statement: For a DVR O, an irreducible pi, a commutative O-algebra A and a prime ideal q of A not containing pi_A, the coefficient map O -> A/q is injective. Finiteness and localness of A are unnecessary for this implication.
hypotheses: The image of pi is tested in q under the actual coefficient map.
The quotient uses the prime ideal q, so it is a nontrivial domain.
proofSteps: The kernel of O -> A/q is q contracted to O, which is a prime ideal.
A DVR has precisely one nonzero prime ideal, its maximal ideal (pi). If this contraction were nonzero, it would contain pi, contrary to the hypothesis. Hence the kernel is zero.
Translate zero kernel to injectivity of the ring homomorphism; retain the quotient coefficient map for the following scalar towers.
acceptance: For A=O and q=0 this is the original coefficient injection.
For A=O/(pi), its zero prime contains pi_A=0, so the hypothesis is rejected.
For O[t]/(t^2-pi*t), the two primes (t) and (t-pi) give two separate generic quotient maps, not a canonical chosen point.

nodes.title: Algebraic point with prescribed generic kernel
nodes.statement: Let O be a commutative domain, A a module-finite commutative O-algebra, Omega an algebraically closed field with an injective O-algebra structure, and q a prime of A for which O -> A/q is injective. There is an O-algebra homomorphism f:A -> Omega with kernel exactly q.
hypotheses: Omega need not be a completion and need not be finite over Frac(O).
Use the chosen coefficient action on Omega and the quotient-induced action on A/q.
proofSteps: Put B=A/q. Its finite O-generating family is the image of one for A, hence B is integral and algebraic over O. Since B and Omega are domains and their O maps are injective, both O-module actions are torsion-free.

Apply the pinned IsAlgClosed.lift to B, not to A. Its inspected definition passes through Frac(B) and an embedding of Frac(B) into Omega over Frac(O). Both field maps and B -> Frac(B) are injective, so this particular lift is injective. Do not infer injectivity merely from the source being a domain.
Compose the lift with the quotient A -> B. Injectivity of the lift identifies the composite kernel with q; all coefficient identities follow from composition of the actual algebra maps.
acceptance: A=O[t]/(t^2) with q=(t) maps t to zero; the point need not be injective on A.
A product algebra can have several generic kernels. The statement constructs one point for the specified q, not an embedding of every finite algebra.
The coefficient injection into B is essential: a characteristic-p quotient cannot map as an O-algebra into a characteristic-zero Omega.

nodes.title: Finite field generated by point values
nodes.statement: Let O be a commutative ring, K a field, and Omega a field in a compatible O -> K -> Omega scalar tower. For a module-finite commutative O-algebra A and an O-algebra homomorphism f:A -> Omega, the intermediate field E=K(f(A)) inside Omega is finite-dimensional over K. No injectivity or reducedness of A is assumed.
hypotheses: E is the existing IntermediateField.adjoin of the range of f, not a private field-of-values carrier.
Finiteness means module-finite A/O, not merely finitely generated A as an algebra.
proofSteps: Use Module.Finite.exists_fin' to choose a finite O-generating family a_i. Let W be the K-linear span in Omega of the f(a_i). Every f(a) lies in W by the O-linear expression for a and the coefficient compatibility of f.

The subspace W contains 1 and is closed under multiplication: expand a_i*a_j in the same O-generators, apply f, and then use K-bilinearity. Consequently W underlies a finite-dimensional K-subalgebra C of Omega.

C is integral over the field K by the finite/integral theorem. Algebra.IsIntegral.inv_mem shows it is closed under inverses in Omega, so the same subset defines an intermediate field. It contains f(A); conversely any intermediate field containing f(A) contains W. Thus this field is exactly E, which inherits the finite spanning family.
acceptance: For A=O the field of point values is K.
A finite nonreduced algebra such as O[t]/(t^2) gives E=K under t->0.
The hypothesis cannot be replaced by finite type: evaluation of O[t] at a transcendental element in a larger field generates an infinite-dimensional extension.

nodes.title: Characteristic-zero integral points
nodes.statement: Let O be a DVR with fraction field K of characteristic zero; let Omega be a chosen algebraically closed extension of K, with the compatible O action. Let A be a commutative local O-algebra finite as an O-module, with 1 <= ringKrullDim(A). Then some finite intermediate field E/K in Omega admits an O-algebra map A -> integralClosure(O,E) that reflects units, and this integral closure is finite over O. No fixed target residue field or topology is asserted by this algebraic theorem. The complete-local-field interpretation and framed lifting remain distinct required extensions recorded below, not premises of this result.
hypotheses: The algebraic core only assumes a DVR, not completeness or a finite residue field. The ring-of-integers/topological interpretation uses the stated complete local-field supplier.
Do not replace positive dimension by A nonzero. Do not require A to be flat or torsion-free.
The integrated node ID is retained; its combined argument is refined into the four preceding nodes and this assembly.
proofSteps: Choose a uniformizer pi. If pi_A were nilpotent, nilpotent-uniformizer-artinian would make A Artinian. All its primes would be maximal, hence ringKrullDim(A)<=0 by the pinned dimension characterization, contradicting the premise.

Negate nilpotent_iff_mem_prime to select q prime avoiding pi_A. Apply generic-prime-coefficient-injection and algebraic-point-of-generic-prime to obtain f:A -> Omega with kernel q. The field E=K(f(A)) is finite by finite-field-of-point-values.

Corestrict f to E using its range inclusion and the induced O action. Each value is integral over O because A/O is finite, so corestrict once more to the existing integralClosure(O,E). In characteristic zero E/K is separable. IsIntegralClosure.finite applies since a DVR is Noetherian and integrally closed, showing that this closure is finite over O.

The map factors through an injective map B=A/q -> integralClosure(O,E). Every target element is integral over O and therefore over B by tower_top. RingHom.IsIntegral.isLocalHom makes that injective map reflect units. The quotient A -> B is local by IsLocalHom.of_surjective, and their composite is local by RingHom.isLocalHom_comp. The integral-injective lemma is NOT applied directly to A -> target, which generally has a kernel.
acceptance: A=O/(pi^n)[t]/(t^2) is finite and nonzero but has dimension zero, so is correctly rejected.
A=O[t]/(pi*t,t^2) has the point t->0 despite its nonzero pi-torsion. Flatness is not required.
A=O[t]/(t^2-pi*t) has the two points t->0 and t->pi, which can coincide on the special fiber. No uniqueness or special-fiber separation is asserted.

For O=Z_3 and A=O[t]/(t^2-18), any integral characteristic-zero point makes t/3 an integral unit whose square is 2. Its residue cannot lie in F_3. Thus a fixed-residue-field strengthening is not a general finite-algebra theorem. This is not an allegation that the source arithmetic corollary is false.
Without module-finiteness, A=k[t] viewed as an O-algebra has dimension one but pi acts by zero; the theorem must reject this example.

nodes.title: Catenary rings
nodes.statement: A commutative ring R is catenary if for all prime ideals p ⊆ q (i) there is an integer bounding the lengths of all chains of primes p = p_0 ⊊ p_1 ⊊ ... ⊊ p_e = q, and (ii) any two saturated chains from p to q (chains in which each step p_i ⊊ p_{i+1} is a covering relation, no prime strictly between) have the same length. Chains are LTSeries in the poset PrimeSpectrum R; a saturated chain has every step a covering relation ⋖.
hypotheses: No Noetherian or local hypothesis in the definition.
The boundedness clause is part of the definition (Stacks 00NI); for a Noetherian ring it is automatic, since chains from p to q have length at most ht q < ∞.
proofSteps: Definition: Ring.IsCatenary R := for all p ≤ q in PrimeSpectrum R, (∃ n, every LTSeries from p to q has length ≤ n) ∧ (any two LTSeries from p to q whose steps are all covering relations have equal length).
acceptance: Saturation matters: k[x, y] is catenary although 0 ⊂ (x, y) and 0 ⊂ (x) ⊂ (x, y) have different lengths; only the second is saturated.
The equal-length clause is not automatic for Noetherian local domains: Nagata's ring A[x]_{m'} (Stacks 02JE) has dimension 3 and a maximal chain (0) ⊂ pA[x]_{m'} ⊂ m' of length 2.
Boundedness is part of the definition: for Noetherian rings it holds by finiteness of heights, so the clause only restricts non-Noetherian rings.

uses.how: Taylor's Lemma 2.2(2) assumes A catenary; R03.6 states it in the dimension-function form, which catenary-iff-dimension-function identifies with this predicate for Noetherian local rings.
'explicit catenarity and excellence hypotheses rather than geometric conclusions for arbitrary local rings'.

nodes.title: Catenarity of a Noetherian local ring as a dimension function
nodes.statement: Let (A, m) be a Noetherian local ring. Then A is catenary if and only if dim A/p = dim A/q + 1 for all primes p ⋖ q of A (q covers p: p ⊊ q with no prime strictly between). Here dim is ringKrullDim of the quotient ring.
hypotheses: A Noetherian and local, so dim A is finite.
The right-hand side is exactly the hypothesis hcat of R03.6's NearlyFaithful.of_quotient_of_isSMulRegular.
proofSteps: For a prime p, dim A/p is the Krull dimension of the poset V(p) of primes containing p (Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient), and it is finite because dim A/p ≤ dim A < ∞ (Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient_le and ringKrullDim_lt_top, the FiniteRingKrullDim instance for Noetherian local rings in KrullsHeightTheorem). So every chain of primes starting at p has length at most dim A/p (Mathlib Order.LTSeries.length_le_krullDim), and some chain of length dim A/p starts at p; since m contains every prime, it may be taken to end at m.

A chain of maximal length between two primes is saturated: otherwise inserting a prime strictly between two consecutive terms (Mathlib RelSeries.insertNth) gives a longer chain. Hence there is a saturated chain from p to m of length dim A/p.

(⇒) Let p ⋖ q. By the second step there is a saturated chain from q to m of length dim A/q; putting p in front gives a saturated chain from p to m of length dim A/q + 1. There is also a saturated chain from p to m of length dim A/p. By the equal-length clause of catenary, dim A/p = dim A/q + 1.

(⇐) Boundedness: by the first step, any chain from p to q has length at most dim A/p < ∞. Equal lengths: along a saturated chain p = p_0 ⋖ p_1 ⋖ ... ⋖ p_e = q the hypothesis gives dim A/p_i = dim A/p_{i+1} + 1, so e = dim A/p − dim A/q, which does not depend on the chain.
acceptance: Locality is needed: let A be k[x, y] localized at the complement of (x, y) ∪ (x − 1). By prime avoidance its primes are those of k[x, y] inside (x, y) or inside (x − 1), so A is a catenary Noetherian domain (a localization of k[x, y], Stacks 00NJ) with maximal ideals (x, y)A of height 2 and (x − 1)A of height 1. Then (0) ⋖ (x − 1)A, but dim A/(0) = 2 while dim A/(x − 1)A = 0.

Catenary does not give equidimensional: A = k⟦x, y, z⟧/(xz, yz) (a plane and a line through the closed point) satisfies the dimension-function condition, e.g. (x, y) ⋖ m with 1 = 0 + 1 and (z) ⋖ (x, z) with 2 = 1 + 1, yet its minimal primes have dimensions 2 and 1. R03.6's lifting lemma therefore keeps its separate equidimensionality hypothesis.
On Nagata's ring A[x]_{m'} (Stacks 02JE) the condition fails along (0) ⋖ pA[x]_{m'} ⋖ m': dim of the ring is 3, so dim A/(0) = 3, while dim along the saturated chain is 2.

uses.how: R03.6 requested this equivalence (its request to R03.3, Stacks 0ECF) so that Taylor's catenarity hypothesis can be stated as a predicate; its Lean hypothesis hcat is the right-hand side.

sources.locator: Algebra, Lemma 10.105.10, tag 0ECF
sources.excerpt: Let (A, m) be a Noetherian local ring. The following are equivalent: (1) A is catenary, and (2) p ↦ dim(A/p) is a dimension function on Spec(A).
sources.match: Exactly this equivalence; for p ↦ dim A/p the strict-decrease clause of a dimension function is automatic, so (2) is the covering condition stated here. Stacks proves it through Topology Lemmas 5.20.2 and 5.20.4; the proof here is the direct chain argument.

nodes.title: A regular local ring has a regular sequence of length its dimension
nodes.statement: Let A be a regular local ring of dimension d. Then every minimal set of generators x_1, ..., x_d of the maximal ideal is an A-regular sequence; in particular A has an A-regular sequence in m of length d = ringKrullDim A, so A is Cohen–Macaulay (depth A = dim A).
hypotheses: A regular local: Noetherian local with m generated by dim A elements (Mathlib IsRegularLocalRing).
proofSteps: Induction on d. For d = 0 the empty sequence works.
For d > 0, A is a domain (gap: Stacks 00NP, via the associated graded ring of 00NO), so x_1 ≠ 0 is a nonzerodivisor; x_1 ∈ m.

Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient_span_singleton_succ_eq_ringKrullDim_of_mem_nonZeroDivisors gives dim A/(x_1) = d − 1, and the images of x_2, ..., x_d generate the maximal ideal of A/(x_1). So A/(x_1) is regular local of dimension d − 1 (Mathlib isRegularLocalRing_iff: a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal is generated by dim elements), and by induction x_2, ..., x_d is A/(x_1)-regular. Hence x_1, ..., x_d is A-regular (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular unfolds as x_1 regular followed by a regular sequence on the quotient).
acceptance: Regularity is needed: A = k⟦x, y⟧/(x², xy) is Noetherian local of dimension 1, but the nonzero element x is killed by the whole maximal ideal (x, y), so every element of m is a zero divisor and A has no regular sequence of length 1.
The converse fails: k⟦x, y⟧/(xy) has dimension 1 and the regular element x + y, so it is Cohen–Macaulay, but its maximal ideal needs two generators, so it is not regular.
Dimension one: for a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ, the sequence (ϖ) is regular of length 1.

uses.how: depth A = dim A enters the Auslander–Buchsbaum computation pd M = depth A − depth M = 0.

sources.locator: Algebra, Lemma 10.106.3, tag 00NQ
sources.excerpt: Let R be a regular local ring and let x_1, ..., x_d be a minimal set of generators for the maximal ideal m. Then x_1, ..., x_d is a regular sequence, and each R/(x_1, ..., x_c) is a regular local ring of dimension d − c. In particular R is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Maximal-depth modules over a regular local ring are free
nodes.statement: Let A be a regular local ring and M a finite A-module that has an M-regular sequence r_1, ..., r_n in the maximal ideal of length n = dim A (that is, M ≠ 0 and depth M ≥ dim A: M is maximal Cohen–Macaulay). Then M is free.
hypotheses: A regular local ring (Mathlib IsRegularLocalRing).
M finite over A; the regular sequence lies in m and has length ringKrullDim A. RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular includes M/(r)M ≠ 0, so M ≠ 0.
Stated with a regular sequence because the pinned Mathlib has no module depth; this is the form R03.6 uses.
proofSteps: depth M ≥ dim A from the given sequence, and depth M ≤ dim Supp M ≤ dim A by the integrated R03.3 node; so depth M = dim A = d, and M ≠ 0 (Mathlib RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular.nontrivial).
A regular local ring has finite global dimension (the integrated R03.3 node), so pd_A M < ∞.
depth A = d by regular-local-cohen-macaulay.
Auslander–Buchsbaum (the integrated R03.3 node) gives pd_A M + depth M = depth A, so pd_A M = 0: M is projective.
A finite projective module is flat (Mathlib instance Module.Flat.of_projective), and a finite flat module over a local ring is free (Mathlib Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing).
acceptance: Regularity of A is needed: over the dual numbers k[ε] (dimension 0) the empty sequence has length 0 = dim, but k = k[ε]/(ε) is not free.
Maximal depth is needed: over k⟦x⟧ (regular, dimension 1), k = k⟦x⟧/(x) has depth 0 and is not free.

Compatibility with ModularCurves 4D (required by RS-08): for a finite local homomorphism A → B of regular local rings of the same dimension d, a regular system of parameters of B is a B-regular sequence of length d (regular-local-cohen-macaulay); together with a system of parameters of A it shows depth_A B = d, so B is free over A. This recovers 4D's miracle flatness for finite maps of regular local rings of equal dimension rather than restating it.

nodes.title: Hilbert–Samuel quotient-length function
nodes.statement: For any commutative ring A, module M and ideal q, define H(q,M,n)=length_A(M/(q^(n+1)·M)) in ℕ∞. Here q^(n+1)·M is the existing ideal action on the top submodule. For the local Noetherian finite-module regime, finite-adic-quotient-length proves that these values are finite; only then read them in ℕ or ℚ.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring and M an A-module for this raw extended-natural-valued definition; q is any ideal.
proofSteps: Use the actual quotient of M by (q^(n+1))·top, with its induced A action. Use Module.length directly, not the number of elements, a residue-field dimension of the whole quotient, or an unproved length-toNat conversion.
acceptance: At n=0 take M/qM, not the zero quotient M/M.
A finite quotient over an infinite residue field can still have finite length.

nodes.title: Finite length under maximal-ideal-power annihilation
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local A and finite A-module N, if m^r·N=0 for some r:ℕ, then length_A(N)≠∞, including r=0 and N=0.
hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring, N a finite A-module.
There is r:ℕ such that m^r·top_N=bottom.
proofSteps: Filter N by m^iN for 0≤i≤r. Each subquotient is finite, because A is Noetherian, and is annihilated by m.

Use the induced A/m scalar action on each subquotient. Module.length_eq_of_surjective compares its A-length with its residue-field length, and Module.length_eq_finrank makes the latter a finite natural number.

Induct along the finite filtration using Module.length_eq_add_of_exact on the actual inclusion/projection exact sequences; do not assume they split. For r=0 the annihilation hypothesis already makes N zero.
acceptance: The module k[ε]/(ε²) has length 2 over itself although the filtration need not split.
Without finite generation an infinite direct sum of k has mN=0 but infinite length.

nodes.statement: Under the common hypotheses, H(q,M,n)≠∞ for every n:ℕ.
hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; q is an ideal with radical q = m.

proofSteps: Use Ideal.exists_radical_pow_le_of_fg and Noetherianity to choose r with m^r⊆q. If needed increase r to a positive integer; ideal powers decrease.
The quotient N=M/q^(n+1)M is finite and is annihilated by m^(r(n+1)), since m^(r(n+1))⊆q^(n+1). Apply finite-length-of-maximal-power-annihilation.
This supplies the necessary finiteness witness before H.toNat is interpreted as the genuine length.

For k[[x,y]], q=(x) is rejected: its radical is not m, and A/q^(n+1) has infinite length.

nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of the cumulative polynomial
nodes.statement: Under the common hypotheses there is exactly one P∈ℚ[T] such that P(n)=H(q,M,n).toNat for all n≥N for some N:ℕ. The polynomial interpolates the cumulative function, not the degree-n graded piece.
hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; q is an ideal with radical q = m.
M is a finite A-module; no field, DVR, equidimensionality, completeness, freeness or nonzero hypothesis unless explicitly stated.
proofSteps: The associated-graded ring/module gap supplies gr_q(A), gr_q(M), multiplication, Noetherianity, degree-one ring generation and finite graded-module generation. Its degree-n carrier is the native G_n in graded-hilbert-function; no increasing word-filtration carrier is substituted.

The remaining graded numerical-polynomial theorem follows the inspected induction of Stacks 10.58.7: stabilize the largest x-power-torsion submodule, terminate its nilpotent filtration, and prove the shifted degree-one multiplication exact sequences before induction on generators. This supplies Q∈ℚ[T] and N with Q(i)=φ(q,M,i).toNat for i≥N. These are still recorded gaps, not consequences of Polynomial.hilbertPoly.

Finite-graded-piece-length validates every coefficient conversion. Apply cumulative-polynomial-from-graded-tail to Q,N: P=S(Q)+Σ_{i<N}(φ(i).toNat−Q(i)) is the cumulative polynomial on n≥N. The new cumulative length and rational summation nodes account for this entire step; the finite initial constant is retained.
Uniqueness uses Polynomial.eq_of_infinite_eval_eq on the infinite tail of distinct rational natural-number casts. Finite-adic-quotient-length validates the cumulative values.
acceptance: For O a DVR and q=m, P=T+1, not T and not the constant 1.
For the embedded-prime example P=T+2 agrees only for n≥1; P(0)=2 is not the actual H(0)=1.

nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local A, ideal q with radical q=m and finite M, define P(q,M) to be the unique polynomial of eventual-hilbert-samuel-polynomial. Its coefficient field is ℚ. hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; q is an ideal with radical q = m.

nodes.title: Polynomial degree equals support dimension
nodes.statement: For a nonzero finite M and radical q=m, P(q,M)≠0 and the natural degree d of P satisfies Module.supportDim A M=d (in WithBot ℕ∞). For M=0, P=0 and both polynomial degree and support dimension are −∞; no artificial dimension-zero convention is imposed.
hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; q is an ideal with radical q = m.
M is a finite A-module; no field, DVR, equidimensionality, completeness, freeness or nonzero hypothesis unless explicitly stated.
proofSteps: For q=m the dimension bridge gap supplies the exact-sequence leading-degree comparison of Stacks 10.59.10 and the local-ring degree/dimension theorem 10.60.9. Apply the existing prime-filtration theorem, not a new filtration construction.

In a prime filtration, degree equals the maximum degree of its factors and support is the union of their closed supports. Stacks 10.62.6 identifies these maxima. Module.supportDim is the existing dimension carrier, and Module.supportDim_eq_ringKrullDim_quotient_annihilator pins its convention.

For another ideal of definition q, compare powers of q and m as in Stacks10.59.4 and10.59.7; polynomial growth in both directions gives the same degree. The nonzero-hilbert-samuel-polynomial node independently rules out the zero polynomial, without using this degree comparison.
Use Module.supportDim_eq_bot_iff_subsingleton for the zero branch, not natDegree(0)=0 as a dimension assertion.
acceptance: For a DVR O and M=κ(O), degree is zero although dim O=1.
For M=0 keep bottom support dimension.

nodes.title: Factorial top coefficient from finite differences
nodes.statement: For P∈ℚ[T], d:ℕ with natDegree P≤d, and t∈ℚ, Σ_{i=0}^d (−1)^i binom(d,i)P(t−i)=d!·coeff(P,d). This includes P=0 and the case natDegree P<d.
hypotheses: P is a rational polynomial, d a natural number bounding its natural degree, and t a rational number.
proofSteps: Induct on the number of backward differences ΔP(T)=P(T)−P(T−1); Pascal's identity gives the binomial expression.

For positive polynomial degree, Δ lowers degree by one and multiplies the leading coefficient by that degree, by binomial expansion. A constant has zero first difference; the zero polynomial remains zero.
After d steps obtain d! coeff(P,d). This proof is polynomial algebra only; it does not assume that module lengths themselves are exact-sequence additive at every adic level.
acceptance: For P=(T+1)(T+2)/2 and d=2 the difference equals 1, not 1/2.
For P=T+1 and d=2 it equals 0.

nodes.title: Intrinsic Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local A, radical q=m and finite A-module M, define e(q;M)∈ℚ by natDegree(P(q,M))! times the leading coefficient of P(q,M). Set e(M)=e(m;M) and e(A)=e(m;A). This gives e(q;0)=0 without assigning the zero module dimension zero. For nonzero M, hilbert-samuel-degree identifies the factorial index with dim Supp M. A separate theorem proves this rational value is a positive integer.
hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; q is an ideal with radical q = m.
M is a finite A-module; no field, DVR, equidimensionality, completeness, freeness or nonzero hypothesis unless explicitly stated.
proofSteps: Use the actual cumulative polynomial and its top coefficient. The zero polynomial has zero leading coefficient, so the formula is zero even though its natural degree is zero.
Do not redefine a curve multiplicity or ambient-normalized module multiplicity here: curve applications specialize to M=A=O_C,x; ambient normalization uses multiplicityInDegree at dim A.

The definition is general in the ideal q and finite module M. Its existence theorem and support-degree comparison carry recorded gaps; merely giving the reserved id does not certify key-definition closure.
acceptance: The intrinsic multiplicity of κ(O) over a DVR O is 1, while its ambient-normalized multiplicity is 0.
The embedded-prime example has multiplicity 1 but is not regular.

proofSteps: Let d=natDegree P. For t a sufficiently large natural integer, all t−i (0≤i≤d) are above the eventual evaluation threshold. top-coefficient-finite-difference expresses e as an integer linear combination of genuine integer quotient lengths, proving integrality.

nodes.title: Multiplicity for powers of an ideal of definition
nodes.statement: For s>0 and nonzero finite M of support dimension d, e(q^s;M)=s^d e(q;M). For M=0 both sides vanish.
hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; q is an ideal with radical q = m.
M is a finite A-module; no field, DVR, equidimensionality, completeness, freeness or nonzero hypothesis unless explicitly stated.
proofSteps: The actual quotient functions satisfy H(q^s,M,n)=H(q,M,s(n+1)−1) for every n; the exponent identity is s(n+1).
For sufficiently large n, polynomial evaluation identifies P(q^s,M) with P(q,M) composed with sT+(s−1), by uniqueness.
The coefficient of degree d of this composition is s^d times the original top coefficient by the binomial theorem. Multiply by d!, using hilbert-samuel-degree and radical(q^s)=radical(q) for s>0.

nodes.title: Additivity at a common dimension
nodes.statement: For a short exact sequence 0→M'→M→M''→0 of finite A-modules, q with radical q=m, and d:ℕ with Module.supportDim A M≤d, e(q;M,d)=e(q;M',d)+e(q;M'',d). Consequently intrinsic multiplicity is additive if all nonzero terms have the same dimension; it is not asserted additive for mixed dimensions.
hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; q is an ideal with radical q = m.
M is a finite A-module; no field, DVR, equidimensionality, completeness, freeness or nonzero hypothesis unless explicitly stated.
proofSteps: The Artin–Rees leading-coefficient gap supplies the correctly filtered quotient exact sequence: kernel M'/(M'∩q^(n+1)M), not generally M'/q^(n+1)M'.

Use Stacks 10.59.3 to replace the intersection filtration by a shifted q-adic filtration of a finite-colength submodule N⊆M'. The finite-colength comparison 10.59.9 preserves top coefficients in positive dimension.

Stacks 10.59.10 shows the discrepancy has strictly smaller degree; when M' has finite length, Artin–Rees makes its intersection with q^nM vanish eventually and the discrepancy becomes exactly length M'. Thus the dimension-zero case is genuine length additivity, not an omitted case.
Extract the coefficient of degree d of the eventual polynomials; terms of smaller dimension have zero dth coefficient by hilbert-samuel-degree. Multiply by d!.

The sum is finite; localized lengths are finite. At d=dim M≠−∞ this gives intrinsic associativity. Primes outside Supp M are not assigned ∞·0 terms.
hypotheses: A is a commutative Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m; q is an ideal with radical q = m.
M is a finite A-module; no field, DVR, equidimensionality, completeness, freeness or nonzero hypothesis unless explicitly stated.
proofSteps: The finite top-dimensional support/localization gap identifies these primes with the relevant minimal support primes and proves the lengths of localized modules finite, as in Stacks 10.62.5.

Use the existing prime-filtration induction and dimension-normalized-additivity. Do not introduce a new generic filtration. The localized length is additive by the existing length exact-sequence theorem.

On a factor A/r, only p=r of dimension d contributes, with local length 1; if dim(A/r)<d both sides are zero. Transport q to the quotient coefficient ring and compare its lengths using Module.length_eq_of_surjective.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, K in the existing DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R) is perfect exactly when there are a cochain complex C, integers a,b, finite projective R-modules C^i in every degree, vanishing C^i outside [a,b], and an isomorphism Q(C) ≅ K in the derived category. No directed quasi-isomorphism from K to a projective representative is required.
hypotheses: R arbitrary commutative; a localization choice HasDerivedCategory is explicit. No local, complete or Noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use the pinned DerivedCategory.Q and existentially quantify an actual cochain complex, its finite/projective predicates and its termwise interval bound.
acceptance: A nonzero finite projective module in degree n is perfect.
A contractible disk is perfect although its chosen representative has two nonzero terms.

nodes.title: Minimal complexes over local rings
nodes.statement: For a local commutative ring (R,m,κ), a cochain complex C is minimal if every differential has image contained in m C^{i+1}. The predicate itself asserts neither finiteness, freeness nor boundedness. On finite-free complexes this is equivalently zero differentials after tensoring with κ, and equivalently all matrix entries lie in m in any chosen bases.
hypotheses: R local; m is IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R. Use LinearMap.range and ideal action on the actual ModuleCat carriers.
proofSteps: Define IsMinimal C by range(d_i) ≤ m • top; linearity gives the condition at every integer degree.
acceptance: [R --π→R] over a DVR is minimal, but [R --1→R] is not.
The zero complex is minimal.

nodes.title: Cancel a unit in a differential
nodes.statement: Given a complex of finite free R-modules with chosen finite bases, if an entry of d_i:C^i→C^{i+1} is a unit, there is a strict complex isomorphism C ≅ C′ ⊕ D_i(R), where D_i is the identity disk in degrees i,i+1. The ranks in those two degrees drop by one; all other degrees are unchanged. The disk has an explicit contracting homotopy.
hypotheses: R any commutative ring; a unit coefficient is required, not merely a nonzero coefficient. No exactness assumption on C.
proofSteps: Permute the selected row/column and scale the unit to 1. Use elementary basis operations to eliminate the rest of its column and row.
In d_i=diag(1,d′), d_i d_{i−1}=0 forces the incoming component into the selected summand to vanish; d_{i+1} d_i=0 forces the outgoing component to vanish.
Restrict the remaining differentials to complements. The inverse elementary operations assemble a complex isomorphism. Contract D_i by the identity map from degree i+1 to i.
acceptance: Over Z/4, diag(1,2) splits as an identity disk and [R --2→ R].

nodes.title: Minimal representatives
nodes.statement: For a bounded above finite-free complex C over a local ring there exist a bounded above finite-free minimal complex M and a HomotopyEquiv C M. More precisely C is isomorphic to M plus a locally finite direct sum of identity disks: only finitely many disk summands meet any fixed degree. If C is bounded in [a,b], M has the same termwise bound and the disk sum is finite. The construction is not canonical.
hypotheses: R local, C termwise finite free and bounded above; no Noetherianity or completeness. Fix bases and cancellation choices; uniqueness of the output is a separate theorem.
proofSteps: Starting at the upper bound b, cancel all unit entries of d_{b−1}, then d_{b−2}, and continue downwards. At each step the finite rank of the relevant terms strictly decreases.
After a differential has no units, all its coefficients lie in m. Subsequent basis changes preserve this property. Splitting further disks does not introduce coefficients outside m.

For every fixed degree only finitely many steps affect it: stages above it are finite in number and stages below i−1 do not change degree i. Assemble the stabilized terms, maps and inverse maps degreewise; this is an algebraic degreewise construction, not an unproved topological inverse limit.

The canceled disk family is degreewise finite. Its componentwise identity contraction is a defined map in every degree. Projection and inclusion give HomotopyEquiv C M. In the bounded case the sum of all original ranks bounds the number of cancellations.
acceptance: C=[R --1→R] has M=0.
C=[R --π→R] over a DVR is already minimal; both ranks survive even though only H^0(C) is nonzero.
Over k[ε]/ε², the infinite resolution of k stays bounded above and minimal but not bounded below.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of minimal complexes
nodes.statement: Any homotopy equivalence between termwise finite-free minimal complexes over a local ring has a forward map that is a strict isomorphism of cochain complexes. Consequently two bounded above finite-free minimal complexes representing the same derived object are strictly isomorphic. No uniqueness of the isomorphism is asserted.
hypotheses: The first assertion needs no bound. The derived-object assertion needs bounded above termwise projective complexes, so the pinned K-projective comparison applies.
proofSteps: Apply homotopy-residue-equality to the composites fg and gf. Their residual component maps are mutually inverse in every degree.

Apply Module.IsLocalRing.linearCombination_bijective_of_flat in finite bases (or its split-injection form plus residual surjectivity) to each component. A finite-free local map invertible residually is invertible.
Assemble component inverses; f_i d_D=d_C f_{i+1} implies the inverse chain identities by multiplying with these inverses.
For a derived isomorphism between bounded above projective representatives, use isKProjective_of_projective and Qh_map_bijective, then quasiIso_iff, to obtain the required homotopy equivalence.
acceptance: A homotopy equivalence 0→[R --1→R] is not a strict isomorphism; minimality is indispensable.
The identity and multiplication by any unit congruent to 1 modulo m give distinct isomorphisms of a nonzero stalk complex.

nodes.title: Minimal ranks from residual cohomology
nodes.statement: For a termwise finite-free minimal complex M, H^i(M⊗_R κ) ≅ M^i⊗_R κ. Thus rank_R(M^i)=dim_κ H^i(M⊗κ). For bounded above C and its minimal representative M, homotopy invariance identifies the right-hand side with H^i(C⊗κ). In particular M^i=0 iff this residual cohomology is zero.
hypotheses: R local; ordinary termwise tensor of the projective representatives is used. The interpretation as derived base change needs the K-flat comparison recorded separately.
proofSteps: Minimality makes both neighboring residual differentials zero; cycles are the whole term and boundaries are zero.
Choose a finite basis of M^i and tensor it to a κ-basis, giving equality of rank and dimension. A finite-dimensional vector space has dimension zero iff it is zero; Nakayama then gives M^i=0.
Base change a HomotopyEquiv by the pinned mapHomotopyEquiv to preserve residual cohomology.

nodes.title: Exactness from a residual three-term complex
nodes.statement: For finite-free M⁰,M¹,M² over any local ring R, and maps d₀,d₁ with d₁d₀=0, if im(d₀⊗κ)=ker(d₁⊗κ), then im d₀=ker d₁. Moreover ker d₀ splits in M⁰, im d₀ splits in M¹, and im d₁ splits in M². Exactness here is only at M¹; no injectivity at M⁰ or surjectivity at M² is asserted.
hypotheses: R arbitrary commutative local, all three modules finite free, and actual composition zero before reduction. No Noetherianity or completeness.
proofSteps: Choose a κ-basis of ker(d₁⊗κ), and lift preimages through d₀ to vectors x_j in M⁰. Extend d₀(x_j) to a residual basis of M¹.
The resulting finite-free map R^r⊕R^s→M¹ is an isomorphism by the pinned local basis-lifting theorem. Denote the first factor U. It lies in im d₀ and ker d₁.
The induced map M¹/U→M² is injective modulo m by residual exactness. Apply split_injective_iff_lTensor_residueField_injective to split it. Therefore ker d₁=U=im d₀ and im d₁ splits in M².
The chosen x_j define a section of M⁰→U, so its kernel splits in M⁰. U already splits in M¹ by the basis decomposition.
acceptance: Over Z/4, d₀(x)=(x,0), d₁(x,y)=y gives the split exact middle and all three summands.
The zero maps R→0→R satisfy the hypothesis without either endpoint exactness.
Over Z localized at 3 the map multiplication by 2 is invertible; over Z itself, reduction mod 3 of Z --2→Z→0 is exact while the original is not. Locality matters.

nodes.title: Perfect objects are pseudo-coherent
nodes.statement: Every perfect K is pseudo-coherent over an arbitrary commutative ring. A finite-projective representative need not itself have finite-free terms; adding a bounded above locally finite family of contractible disks produces a finite-free representative.
hypotheses: R commutative; no local hypothesis; the resulting free complex can be unbounded below.
proofSteps: Starting at the top, choose a finite-projective complement making the highest projective term finite free.
At each lower degree choose a finite-projective complement making C^i plus the complement from degree i+1 finite free. Put the incoming complement identity into the differential.
The added complements form contractible disks with only two adjacent terms. The projection to C is a homotopy equivalence degreewise. Use the original derived isomorphism and pseudo-coherent-object.

nodes.title: Residual Nakayama for pseudo-coherent objects
nodes.statement: For a pseudo-coherent K over a local commutative ring, K⊗ᴸκ=0 iff K=0. This theorem is not a statement about arbitrary complexes, and does not require derived completeness.

The zero representative gives K=0. The reverse implication is functoriality of base change.
Apply the object assertion to cone(u), using exactness of derived base change and the existing cone criterion for an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Residual acyclicity gives a contraction

nodes.title: Finite perfect approximation of a negative tail
nodes.statement: Let F be a bounded above finite-free cochain complex over a commutative ring and let a be an integer. Its brutal truncation Q=σ_{≥a−1}F is bounded finite free. There is a chain map j:Q→F equal to the identity in degrees ≥a−1. Its quotient complex has terms zero in degrees >a−2. For any E with terms zero in degrees <a, precomposition gives a bijection Hom_D(R)(F,E)→Hom_D(R)(Q,E).
hypotheses: Use brutal truncation for the finite approximation, not the smart truncation: the latter has a cokernel term that need not be projective. F upper bounded; E termwise lower bounded.
proofSteps: Use the pinned stupidTrunc along embeddingUpIntGE(a−1). The inclusion natural transformation is a TODO in that file, so construct j in P7 by identity/zero components and prove its chain-map equation.
Finite free terms and the inherited upper bound make Q perfect. F/Q is strictly ≤a−2.

In the Hom cochain groups of degrees −1,0,1, the only possibly nonzero components F^i→E^{i+n} have i≥a−n. These all lie in Q. Precomposition therefore identifies the three groups and both differentials controlling H⁰.

Use the pinned HomComplex cohomology-to-homotopy comparison and K-projective-to-derived comparison for F and Q. Both are upper bounded projective complexes. This proves the Hom bijection without postulating a generic RHom functor.
acceptance: Over dual numbers, truncate the infinite free resolution of k at a−1; it gives the same degree-zero derived Hom into any complex starting in degree a.
At cutoff a, the degree-one Hom group can lose its i=a−1 component; the extra term is essential to control the cokernel/cocycle condition.

nodes.title: Finite perfect Hom commutes with filtered colimits
nodes.statement: For a bounded finite-projective C and a small filtered diagram E_j of cochain complexes of R-modules, the canonical map colim_j Hom_D(R)(Q(C),Q(E_j))→Hom_D(R)(Q(C),Q(colim_j E_j)) is bijective. The target uses the degreewise complex colimit. No uniform bound on the E_j is needed for this finite source.
hypotheses: R commutative; C termwise finite projective and bounded on both sides; small filtered shape with the required colimits.
proofSteps: A finite-projective module P is a summand of R^r. Hom_R(P,−) is correspondingly a natural summand of the r-fold finite product of the target module, so it commutes with filtered colimits.

Each degree of the existing linear Hom complex from C is a finite product of those functors: C has a fixed finite interval of nonzero terms. The canonical comparison is an isomorphism of Hom complexes, with the signed differential unchanged.
Filtered colimits in ModuleCat are exact by the pinned AB5 instance; taking H⁰ therefore commutes. Use the existing linearHomComplex comparison to Mathlib and its cohomology classes.
Use the pinned K-projective comparison to interpret those classes as derived morphisms.
acceptance: For C=R[0], this is ordinary cohomology commuting with a filtered colimit of module complexes.
A bounded complex with an infinite-free term is not enough: Hom from ⊕_nR is an infinite product and can fail to commute with filtered colimits.

nodes.title: Functorial lower-bounded target replacement
nodes.statement: For a filtered diagram E_j of module complexes with H^i(E_j)=0 for every i<a and one fixed a, the smart truncations τ_{≥a}E_j form a diagram of complexes strictly supported ≥a. The natural maps E_j→τ_{≥a}E_j are quasi-isomorphisms, as is the induced map on degreewise filtered colimits. The colimit itself has no cohomology below a.
hypotheses: One common a is required for the final strict-bound comparison. No target termwise finiteness or boundedness above. This is an application of existing smart truncation and exact filtered colimits, not a second truncation construction.
proofSteps: Use CochainComplex.truncGE, truncGEMap, and quasiIso_πTruncGE_iff. Their functoriality supplies the entire truncated diagram, not separately chosen isomorphic objects.
Use ModuleCat AB5 to commute kernels/cokernels and homology with filtered colimits. The colimit of the natural quasi-isomorphisms is a quasi-isomorphism.
The truncated diagram has all terms below a zero, so its degreewise colimit has the same strict lower bound.
acceptance: A family whose lower bounds tend to −∞ does not yield a single strictly lower-bounded colimit.
Smart truncation of [R --π→R] at zero has O/π as its boundary term, unlike its brutal truncation.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent Hom with a uniform lower bound
nodes.statement: Let P be pseudo-coherent over any commutative ring R, and let E_j be a small filtered diagram of module complexes with H^i(E_j)=0 for all i<a, for one common a. Then the canonical map colim_j Hom_D(R)(P,Q(E_j))→Hom_D(R)(P,Q(colim_j E_j)) is bijective. It is natural in P, in the diagram and in compatible diagram maps. In particular every morphism P→Q(colim E_j) factors through some stage; equality of two stage representatives holds at a common later stage.
hypotheses: Pseudo-coherence of P; filteredness and a single uniform cohomological lower bound on every target. No Noetherianity or local hypothesis. The degreewise complex colimit is a model; no arbitrary colimit in a triangulated category is postulated.
proofSteps: Choose a bounded above finite-free F representing P, and transport the canonical comparison through that derived isomorphism.
Replace the target diagram functorially by smart truncations ≥a using lower-bounded-target-replacement. Its colimit remains quasi-isomorphic to the original one.
Apply finite-free-tail-approximation with cutoff a−1. This gives natural Hom bijections from F to its bounded finite-free Q for all truncated stages and their colimit.
Apply finite-perfect-hom-filtered-colimit to Q. Naturality identifies the composite with the canonical map for P.

Surjectivity is stage factorization; injectivity is eventual equality in a filtered set colimit. This is an equality of morphisms in D(R), not a canonical choice of factor or a strict compatible Hecke action.
acceptance: Over k[ε]/ε², P=k[0] and E_n=⊕_{i=0}^n k[i] violate the common lower bound. The colimit Hom map is ⊕_i k→∏_i k and misses the all-ones sequence.
When P is perfect, finite-perfect-hom-filtered-colimit removes the lower-bound hypothesis.
Constant diagrams have their identity Hom comparison; the zero source has the unique zero factorization.

nodes.title: Positive leading coefficient from a natural tail
nodes.statement: Let P∈ℚ[T] be nonzero. If there is N∈ℕ such that P(n)≥0 for every natural n≥N, then leadingCoeff(P)>0. The hypothesis is only on the natural tail, not on every real or rational input; constants are included.
hypotheses: P is a rational polynomial with P≠0; N is a natural number and all natural n≥N have P(n)≥0.
proofSteps: If natDegree P=0, use the pinned constant-polynomial theorem. Evaluation at N makes its constant nonnegative; nonzero leading coefficient makes it positive.
For positive natural degree, suppose the leading coefficient is nonpositive. The pinned polynomial theorem gives P(x)→−∞ as rational x→+∞.
Compose with the pinned natural-cast limit to get P(n)→−∞. Beyond some natural threshold P(n)<0, contradicting the nonnegative tail at the maximum of the two thresholds.
This proves a strict sign, not integrality or an exact evaluation formula. The zero polynomial cannot be admitted.

M is a finite A-module; no field, DVR, equidimensionality, completeness, freeness or nonzero hypothesis unless explicitly stated.

proofSteps: For I=q^(n+1), positive powers satisfy I⊆q⊆m. If I·M=M, the native finite-submodule Nakayama theorem applies to top: I is inside the Jacobson radical of its annihilator by maximalIdeal_le_jacobson. It would make M zero, a contradiction.
The native quotient nontriviality criterion makes M/I·M nontrivial. Module.length_pos gives strictly positive extended length.
The existing finite-adic-quotient-length node excludes infinity. Only now use ENat.toNat_pos, keeping its two separate premises.

nodes.title: Length of one adic quotient transition
nodes.statement: Put L_n=length_A(M/q^nM), so L_0=0. For every n, L_(n+1)=φ(q,M,n)+L_n in ℕ∞, with no finite-length hypothesis. This comes from 0→G_n→M/q^(n+1)M→M/q^nM→0.

The native inclusion theorem gives injectivity and range(j_n)=F_n.map(mkQ F_(n+1)). Submodule.ker_mapQ applied to the identity map gives this same submodule as ker(π_n). Submodule.factor_surjective gives surjectivity. Hence the range/kernel criterion gives Function.Exact j_n π_n.
Apply Module.length_eq_add_of_exact. No section, direct-sum decomposition or finite natural subtraction is used.

nodes.title: Normalized rational summation polynomial
nodes.statement: For P∈ℚ[T], define S(P)=Σ_{j∈support(P)} (coeff_j(P)/(j+1))·(B_(j+1)(T+1)−B_(j+1)(0)), where B_j is the existing Mathlib Bernoulli polynomial. This normalization sums P(0),…,P(n), not P(1),…,P(n), and has S(P)(−1)=0.
hypotheses: P is a rational polynomial. The positive denominator j+1 is inverted in ℚ, not in a general coefficient ring.
proofSteps: Use Polynomial.bernoulli, polynomial substitution, rational constants and a finite coefficient-support sum. No Bernoulli object or binomial-polynomial structure is newly planned.

The native bernoulli_eval_zero fixes the normalization. The native power-sum theorem and coefficient expansion supply the separately named evaluation lemma. The native bernoulli_comp_one_add_X verifies the forward difference.

For uniqueness among polynomials with the same forward difference and value at −1, compare evaluations recursively at 0,1,… and use the pinned infinite-evaluation equality theorem. This is an API characterization, not an assumption used to define S.
acceptance: S(P)(−1)=0 fixes the arbitrary constant before the actual filtration initial segment is restored.

nodes.title: Cumulative polynomial from a graded polynomial tail
nodes.statement: Assume every φ(q,M,i) is finite, and choose Q∈ℚ[T] and N≥0 such that Q(i)=φ(q,M,i).toNat for all i≥N. Set c_N=Σ_{i=0}^{N−1}(φ(q,M,i).toNat−Q(i)) in ℚ, with the sum empty when N=0. Then for every n≥N, (S(Q)+c_N)(n)=H(q,M,n).toNat. All subtractions in c_N take place after rational casts, never as truncated natural subtraction.
hypotheses: A is a commutative ring, M is an A-module, q is any ideal, and n is a natural number. No finiteness or local hypothesis is imposed unless stated.
All graded lengths are finite. Q is supplied with its eventual graded-value equality from N onwards; existence of such Q is not asserted by this theorem.
proofSteps: Use cumulative-natural-length and cast its sum to ℚ. Split the sum over 0,…,n into 0,…,N−1 and N,…,n.
On the latter interval replace φ(i).toNat by Q(i). The difference of the two full sums is exactly c_N, since n≥N. The finite-range splitting and regrouping are ordinary finite-sum algebra.

Apply summatory-polynomial-evaluation to the full sum of Q. Thus S(Q)+c_N has the required eventual cumulative evaluations. No assumption about gr_q(A), graded generation or Hilbert–Serre is hidden here.
acceptance: If φ(0)=1, φ(1)=2 and φ(i)=1 for i≥2, take Q=1,N=2,c_N=1: the cumulative polynomial is T+2, not T+1. At n=0 its value 2 is not the actual cumulative length 1.
For N=0 the correction is zero. For an eventually zero graded function the cumulative polynomial is a constant, not necessarily zero.
For φ(0)=3 and φ(i)=1 for i≥1, Q=1,N=1 gives c_N=2 and the cumulative polynomial T+3.
If φ(0)=1 and φ(i)=3 for i≥1, take Q=3,N=1,c_N=−2: the cumulative polynomial is 3T+1. Truncated natural subtraction would incorrectly set the correction to zero.

nodes.title: Coefficients of the Rees coefficient ideal
nodes.statement: For p∈Rees(q), p∈q Rees(q) if and only if its coefficient in every degree n belongs to q^(n+1).
hypotheses: A is an arbitrary commutative ring with identity, q is any ideal, and degrees are natural numbers. No local, Noetherian, domain or proper-ideal premise is imposed unless explicitly stated.
proofSteps: The mapped ideal is the span of constant images of elements of q. An ideal-span induction shows each product C(a)p has coefficient a·p_n∈q·q^n=q^(n+1); sums preserve the condition.

Conversely expand p into finitely many monomials. For p_n∈q^(n+1)=q·q^n, use smul_induction_on to express it as a finite sum of a·b with a∈q,b∈q^n. Each monomial is C(a) times the native degree-n Rees monomial bT^n. Sum the expressions over the finite polynomial support. This uses no finite generation of q.
acceptance: Use q^(n+1), not q^n, in the denominator criterion.

nodes.statement: The existing direct-sum linear map Σ_nι_n:⊕_(n≥0)G_n→Gr_q(A) is bijective. Only finitely supported sums occur.

Choices are finite and only prove the comparison, not a new ring carrier.

hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q is any ideal, M is any A-module, and degrees are natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain or freeness premise unless explicitly added.
proofSteps: A native quotient class is zero exactly when its representative belongs to its denominator. Apply the coefficient-denominator criterion to single_n(m).
Submodule.mem_smul_top_iff identifies membership in q·top_F_n with membership of the underlying element in q·F_n; associativity of ideal action identifies this with q^(n+1)M.
acceptance: At degree zero the kernel is qM.
No quotient of M by an incorrectly typed subtype denominator is formed.

nodes.title: The same graded ring acts in the sum of degrees
nodes.statement: For a∈q^r and m∈q^nM, a·m∈q^(r+n)M and μ_r(a)·ν_n(m)=ν_(r+n)(a·m). The action is the native action of the already defined Gr_q(A), not an independently chosen action on a direct sum.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q is any ideal, M is any A-module, and degrees are natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain or freeness premise unless explicitly added.
proofSteps: Use the product of ideal powers and associativity of their action to place a·m in q^(r+n)M.
Use the native PolynomialModule.monomial_smul_single at degrees r,n, then Module.Quotient.mk_smul_mk. Both sides use exactly the existing ring quotient and new module quotient.

nodes.title: Bijective finite homogeneous expansion of the adic module
nodes.statement: The native A-linear direct-sum expansion Σ_nι^M_n:⊕_nG_n→Gr_q(M) is bijective.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q is any ideal, M is any A-module, and degrees are natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain or freeness premise unless explicitly added.
proofSteps: Surjectivity: lift a quotient class to f∈Rq(M), expand its finite coefficient support, and project each single_n(coeff_n f) through ι^M_n.

Injectivity: choose representatives for the finitely many nonzero degree classes. If their expansion is zero, its finite polynomial sum belongs to J·top. The coefficient-denominator criterion and monomial kernel theorem put every degree representative in its own denominator, so every coordinate is zero. No infinite product or convergence assertion is used.
acceptance: Only finite support is involved.
For q=A both sides vanish.

nodes.title: Degree-zero generation descends to the graded module
nodes.statement: For any A,q,M, the Gr_q(A)-submodule spanned by the range of ν_0 is all of Gr_q(M). No finiteness premise is required.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q is any ideal, M is any A-module, and degrees are natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain or freeness premise unless explicitly added.
proofSteps: Apply the native Filtration.submodule_eq_span_le_iff_stable_ge with n₀=0 to the stable adic filtration. Its stability holds in every degree by q·q^nM=q^(n+1)M. F_0=top_M. This existing theorem generates Rq(M) by native degree-zero singles.

Project a finite spanning expression through the actual quotient map. Its coefficients descend from Rq to Rq/J and each degree-zero generator maps to ν_0. Surjectivity gives the stated top-submodule equality.
acceptance: Zero and unit ideals are included.
Generation uses the degree-zero module, not the ring degree-one generating set.

nodes.title: Finite generation of the adic graded module
nodes.statement: If M is finite over A, then Gr_q(M) is finite as a module over Gr_q(A), for any q. A need not be Noetherian and q need not be finitely generated.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q is any ideal, M is any A-module, and degrees are natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain or freeness premise unless explicitly added.
proofSteps: Choose a finite A-spanning set of M from Module.Finite. Since F_0=top_M, A-linearity of ν_0 shows that its full range is in the Gr_q(A)-span of the images of this finite set.

Use adic-module-degree-zero-generation to identify that finite span with top. This proves finite generation over Gr_q(A). No claim that each F_n is finite over A is needed; that stronger component finiteness requires separate hypotheses.
acceptance: This statement does not need the Noetherian component assumption of the existing general filtration FG criterion.
A residue module over Z/4 provides a finite nonfree example.

nodes.title: The regular-module specialization is the same graded ring
nodes.statement: For M=A there exists a Gr_q(A)-linear equivalence Gr_q(A as module)≃Gr_q(A as ring). It sends ν_n(m) to μ_n(m) under the explicit identification q^n·top_A=q^n, so it is compatible with every homogeneous piece.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q is any ideal, M is any A-module, and degrees are natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain or freeness premise unless explicitly added.
proofSteps: The native PolynomialModule.equivPolynomialSelf identifies the polynomial module on A with A[T]. The equality q^n·top_A=q^n follows from Ideal.smul_eq_mul and Ideal.mul_top. Restrict this native polynomial equivalence to the actual Rees-module and Rees-ring subtypes.

This Rees-linear equivalence sends J·top to the ideal J: multiply by 1 for the reverse inclusion, and ideal closure for the forward one. Use Submodule.Quotient.equiv, and the native quotient scalar formula to upgrade the descended equivalence to Rq/J-linearity. Its single-to-monomial formula gives the degree compatibility.
acceptance: For Z/4,q=(2), both regular-module and ring degree-one classes survive.
This comparison is restricted to M=A; it fails for M=A/q when the ring degree-one piece is nonzero.

nodes.title: Homogeneous submodules of the native adic ring
nodes.statement: For the existing quotient S=Rees(q)/(q Rees(q)), define S_n=range(ι_n) as an A-submodule of S. Identify G_n=q^n/(q·top_(q^n)) with S_n by the existing injectivity of ι_n. Compose the inverse finite expansion S→⊕G_n with the direct sum of these range equivalences to obtain the actual A-linear map d:S→⊕S_n.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q any ideal, and degrees natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain or finite-generation premise is required.
proofSteps: Take LinearMap.range of the existing adicPieceInclusion, not a new quotient or abstract component type. LinearEquiv.ofInjective gives e_n:G_n≃range(ι_n), whose underlying value is ι_n.

Define d=(DirectSum.congrLinearEquiv e)∘adicDirectSumEquiv.symm. Both maps use native finitely supported direct sums; no infinite product is allowed. This fixes the candidate decomposition before the native grading is registered.
acceptance: The degree-one class of 2 in gr_(2)(Z/4) survives, while its square vanishes in degree two.
The residue module over Z/4 has only degree zero although the ring has a nonzero positive-degree component.

nodes.title: The native grading of the adic Rees quotient
nodes.statement: Register GradedAlgebra(S_n) on the same S. Its native decomposition is exactly d and its canonical inverse is summation of the submodule inclusions. The unit is in S_0 and S_i S_j⊆S_(i+j). Define π_n:S→S using GradedAlgebra.proj; it is A-linear.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q any ideal, and degrees natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain or finite-generation premise is required.
proofSteps: For the decomposition inverse laws, compare the canonical recomposition with adicDirectSumEquiv composed with the inverse direct-sum range equivalences. The preceding generator identity, range equivalence evaluation and finite linear-map extensionality identify the maps; the inverse laws of the existing linear equivalences finish.

Represent 1 by the constant Rees monomial of coefficient 1∈q^0, hence it belongs to S_0. For multiplication, choose representatives of the two native quotient classes, use adic-homogeneous-product, and descend the representative identity through the quotient. Thus the product belongs to the actual range S_(i+j).

Use these four fields to register GradedRing/GradedAlgebra. Reuse GradedAlgebra.proj for projections and its native decomposition formula. The decomposition identity on ι_j fixes π_i(ι_j x) to ι_j x for i=j and zero otherwise. Homogeneous multiplication then gives the displayed projection product law.
acceptance: The degree-one class of 2 in gr_(2)(Z/4) survives, while its square vanishes in degree two.
The residue module over Z/4 has only degree zero although the ring has a nonzero positive-degree component.

nodes.title: The native grading and action of the adic Rees module
nodes.statement: Register DirectSum.Decomposition(L_n) using d_M and SetLike.GradedSMul(S_n,L_n) using the existing action of S=gr_q(A) on L=gr_q(M). Thus S_i·L_j⊆L_(i+j) for that same action. With the precise native GradedModule.isModule instance, GradedModule.linearEquiv gives L≃ₗ[S]⊕L_n. Define the A-linear ambient projection π_n^M by native decomposition, DFinsupp.lapply and the image-submodule inclusion.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring with identity, q any ideal, M any A-module, and degrees natural numbers. No locality, Noetherianity, proper-ideal, domain, finite-generation or free-module premise is required.
proofSteps: Identify the canonical recomposition with the existing module expansion composed with inverse range equivalences. Check on each lof using the previous homogeneous-decomposition identity and ambient range formula; finite linear extensionality and equivalence inverse laws give both inverse identities required by DirectSum.Decomposition.ofLinearMap.
Import the separately registered native homogeneous scalar-action lemma. The existing quotient action, rather than a transported alternative, is the input to the native external graded action.

Use GradedModule.isModule explicitly for the external direct sum. The native GradedModule.linearEquiv is S-linear, whereas d_M and the individual ambient projections are A-linear. Individual degree projections are generally not S-linear: positive-degree scalars shift degree.

Compose DirectSum.decomposeLinearEquiv with DFinsupp.lapply n and the subtype linear map. The homogeneous inclusion identity gives π_i^M(ι_j^M x)=ι_j^M x if i=j, else zero. The graded scalar law gives π_(i+j)^M(a·x)=a·x for homogeneous inputs.

nodes.title: Variable-ideal powers and total order
nodes.statement: For finite σ, any commutative ring k, R=MvPowerSeries σ k and v=span{X_i | i∈σ}, a series g lies in v^r if and only if (r:ℕ∞)≤order(g), for every r≥0. This includes g=0, r=0, the empty variable set and coefficient rings with zero divisors.
hypotheses: σ is finite, k is any commutative ring, R=MvPowerSeries σ k and v is the algebraically generated ideal span{X_i | i∈σ}. All degrees are natural numbers.
proofSteps: Apply variable-ideal-power-order-bound for the forward implication; its proof works even for an infinite variable set.

For the reverse implication, use finite-degree-monomial-factorization on the native coefficient carrier. Each summand has a coefficient-one degree-r monomial in v^r by monomial-variable-ideal-power, and multiplication by its series factor stays in the same ideal. Closure under the genuinely finite sum proves membership.

No domain, residue-field or local-ring hypothesis is introduced. The zero/zero-power/empty-variable boundaries are handled by the same native proofs. The ideal is algebraically generated; no closure under infinite sums is asserted.

This theorem is now supported by an admission-free native proof prototype. The canonical suggested body stays admitted and the node remains unchecked pending independent review/library implementation. The shifted multiplication, total-jet basis/count, curve length and general multiplicity theorems remain separate open work.
acceptance: For σ=Fin 2, k=ℚ, X_0∈v but X_0∉v².
For k=Z/4 the same membership statement holds although order equality for products can fail.
For the empty variable set and r>0 the only member of v^r is zero.

nodes.title: Shifted jet denominator containment
nodes.statement: With finite σ, commutative k and v as above, let d≤N and (d:ℕ∞)≤order(f). Multiplication by f sends v^(N+1−d) into v^(N+1), equivalently the source submodule is contained in the preimage of the target submodule under the native R-linear multiplication map.
hypotheses: σ is finite, k is any commutative ring, R=MvPowerSeries σ k and v is the algebraically generated ideal span{X_i | i∈σ}. All degrees are natural numbers.
d≤N and (d:ℕ∞)≤order(f). The construction deliberately permits f=0 and d=0; injectivity has stricter separate hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply variable-ideal-power-order to a source element g. The native product-order lower bound gives order(fg)≥order(f)+order(g)≥d+(N+1−d)=N+1 in ENat.
The equality of natural exponents follows from d≤N, so the natural subtraction is legitimate. The zero representative and f=0 are covered directly by extended-natural inequalities.
Apply variable-ideal-power-order to fg. Express the conclusion as Submodule.comap of LinearMap.mulLeft R f, not Ideal.comap: multiplication by f is generally not a ring homomorphism.

Retain the separate variable-ideal-power-order adapter to infer f∈v^d from the order bound. Apply ideal-power-mul-denominator with n=N+1; d≤N implies d≤N+1. This imports the actual ideal-power algebra proof; it does not discharge the order-to-algebraic-ideal bridge.
The current admission-free native prototype applies the proved ideal-power denominator to f∈v^d, using the checked order-to-ideal adapter. The canonical body remains admitted.
acceptance: For d=N the source ideal is v, not v^0.
No no-zero-divisors hypothesis is needed for well-definedness.

nodes.statement: Under d≤N and (d:ℕ∞)≤order(f), construct the actual R-linear map μ_f:R/v^(N+1−d)→R/v^(N+1), [g]↦[fg], by native Submodule.mapQ of LinearMap.mulLeft R f and shifted-jet-denominator. Its projection API is the native factor π_f:R/v^(N+1)→R/((f)+v^(N+1)), [g]↦[g]. No jet carrier, dimension datum, or algebra-homomorphism multiplication stand-in is introduced.
hypotheses: σ is finite, k is any commutative ring, R=MvPowerSeries σ k and v is the algebraically generated ideal span{X_i | i∈σ}. All degrees are natural numbers.
d≤N and (d:ℕ∞)≤order(f). The construction deliberately permits f=0 and d=0; injectivity has stricter separate hypotheses.
proofSteps: Take the displayed actual ideal quotients with their native R-module structures. Descend the native multiplication map using the denominator containment, fixing its value, not merely postulating a map with a type.
Take Submodule.factor for v^(N+1)≤(f)+v^(N+1) as the canonical quotient projection. Its quotient-representative formula is native factor_mk.

Both representative formulas are definitional. Native linearity, map_zero and map_add are inherited from LinearMap; do not re-plan the generic quotient or linear-map APIs. Injectivity, range-kernel identity and small-index behavior are separate lemma nodes below.

nodes.title: Injectivity at the exact equation order
nodes.statement: If σ is finite, k is a commutative ring with no zero divisors, f has exact native order d∈ℕ and d≤N, then the actual shifted jet map μ_f:R/v^(N+1−d)→R/v^(N+1) is injective. Completeness, finite residue field, irreducibility and characteristic-zero hypotheses are unnecessary.
hypotheses: σ is finite, k is any commutative ring, R=MvPowerSeries σ k and v is the algebraically generated ideal span{X_i | i∈σ}. All degrees are natural numbers.
k has no zero divisors, order(f)=(d:ℕ∞), and d≤N. Exact finite order already excludes f=0; d=0 is allowed.
proofSteps: For a representative g of a kernel class, μ_f([g])=0 means fg∈v^(N+1), by the actual representative formula and native quotient equality.

Use the built native MvPowerSeries.order_mul, not a new order-multiplicativity theorem: order(fg)=d+order(g). If g=0 the source class is zero. Otherwise its order is finite and ENat cancellation of the finite d gives order(g)≥N+1−d.
Apply variable-ideal-power-order to get g in the source denominator. Thus the kernel is zero, hence the linear map is injective. Equivalently kernel_mapQ transports the same preimage equality.

An order lower bound alone is insufficient: a series of order larger than d can kill a nonzero source class, even over a field. Over Z/4 take f=2X_0 and g=2: both relevant low classes are nonzero but fg=0.

Apply principal-quotient-injectivity to the actual source and target ideals. Prove its reverse-membership criterion using exact finite order, the built order_mul and the separate variable-ideal-power-order adapter. Right exactness or ambient domain cancellation alone cannot replace this step.

The current admission-free native prototype applies exact-order-mul-ideal-preimage with r=N+1−d, rewrites d+(N+1−d)=N+1 under d≤N, and invokes the proved principal quotient injectivity criterion. Zero representatives need no separate finite-order conversion.

nodes.title: Range and cokernel of shifted jet multiplication
nodes.statement: For finite σ, commutative k, d≤N and (d:ℕ∞)≤order(f), range(μ_f)=ker(π_f) and π_f is surjective, for the exact native maps in shifted-jet-map. Thus R/((f)+v^(N+1)) is their actual cokernel quotient. This right-exact assertion does not require exact finite order or a coefficient domain.
hypotheses: σ is finite, k is any commutative ring, R=MvPowerSeries σ k and v is the algebraically generated ideal span{X_i | i∈σ}. All degrees are natural numbers.
d≤N and (d:ℕ∞)≤order(f). The construction deliberately permits f=0 and d=0; injectivity has stricter separate hypotheses.
proofSteps: Surjectivity is native factor_surjective. A class [h] in the middle quotient lies in the projection kernel exactly when h belongs to (f)+v^(N+1).
For any kernel class choose h=fg+r with r∈v^(N+1), using singleton ideal span membership and the sum-ideal membership criterion. Then [h]=μ_f([g]) for the actual source class, proving kernel⊆range.
Conversely the projection kills every fg because fg∈(f). Native range_mapQ records that the range is the image of the principal ideal under the middle quotient map, yielding the reverse inclusion.

Only after shifted-jet-injective is added under its stricter hypotheses is this a short exact sequence. The further quotient-of-quotient equivalence with A/n^(N+1) and the length/dimension comparisons remain explicit continuation work; do not assert an A-linear structure on the shifted source.

Specialize principal-quotient-exact to A=R,J=v^(N+1−d),K=v^(N+1), using shifted-jet-denominator. The existing shifted map and projection have exactly the same native representative formulas, hence agree by quotient induction. The ring-level exactness proof is now explicit; the series denominator remains the earlier separate prerequisite.

The current native prototype proves equality with quotientMulMap and principalQuotientProjection by their actual definitions, then imports the checked principal-quotient exactness proof. It has no domain or exact-order assumption.

nodes.title: Jets below the equation order
nodes.statement: For finite σ, commutative k, N<d and (d:ℕ∞)≤order(f), one has (f)+v^(N+1)=v^(N+1), and the actual projection π_f:R/v^(N+1)→R/((f)+v^(N+1)) is bijective. This is the small-index branch and asserts no shifted injective multiplication sequence.
hypotheses: σ is finite, k is any commutative ring, R=MvPowerSeries σ k and v is the algebraically generated ideal span{X_i | i∈σ}. All degrees are natural numbers.
N<d and (d:ℕ∞)≤order(f); no domain, nonzero or exact-order hypothesis is required.
proofSteps: Since N+1≤d≤order(f), variable-ideal-power-order gives f∈v^(N+1). The generated principal ideal lies in this power, so their sum is the same power.
The canonical factor under this equality has identical source and target quotient relations. Its representative formula proves injectivity; its native factor_surjective proves surjectivity.

For f=X_0^4,N=0 the projection is the residue-jet bijection, while the tempting multiplication R/v→R/v sends everything to zero. Guard the shifted construction with d≤N and never use truncated natural subtraction to extend injectivity to N<d.

After the existing order-to-ideal adapter establishes f∈v^(N+1), specialize principal-projection-in-ideal. The already planned projection is definitionally the same native factor. No generic bijection theorem is duplicated and no injective shifted map is asserted at small indices.

The current native prototype obtains f∈v^(N+1) from N<d and the order lower bound, then specializes the checked principal projection bijectivity theorem. The small-index example independently rejects a spurious unshifted injection.

nodes.title: Finite degree-monomial factorization
nodes.statement: For finite σ, any commutative ring k, native series g and r∈ℕ with (r:ℕ∞)≤g.order, there is a family h:(σ→₀ℕ)→MvPowerSeries σ k such that g=Σ_{β∈B_r} monomial β 1·h(β), where B_r={β | degree β=r} is the native finite degree fibre. The sum is finite, including r=0 and an empty B_r.
hypotheses: σ is finite; k is any commutative ring, without a domain or nontriviality assumption. g:MvPowerSeries σ k; r∈ℕ; (r:ℕ∞)≤g.order.
proofSteps: Use baseline finite_of_degree_eq to take the finite sum over B_r. For each exponent α of degree at least r, baseline exists_le_degree_eq supplies pick(α)≤α of degree r; below r choose zero. The choice is internal to the proof, not a new public selector or alternate exponent carrier.
On the native coefficient-function carrier define h(β)(γ)=coeff_(β+γ)(g) if pick(β+γ)=β, and zero otherwise. Native ext reduces the asserted finite-sum equality to equality of each coefficient.
If degree α≥r, use coeff_monomial_mul and β+(α−β)=α when β≤α. Exactly the summand β=pick(α) contributes coeff_α(g); every other summand vanishes. Use finite sum_eq_single.

If degree α<r, coeff_of_lt_order makes coeff_α(g)=0. No β∈B_r can satisfy β≤α, by degree_mono; every coefficient of the finite sum is zero. This also proves the empty-variable and r=0 boundaries without separate infinite-series convergence assertions.

hypotheses: R=MvPowerSeries σ k and v=Ideal.span(range(X)); all carriers, powers, coefficient actions, and quotient modules are native library objects.

Kernel/ideal-order adapters require finite σ and CommRing k. The upper branch additionally requires NoZeroDivisors k and exact finite order(f)=d, with d≤n. No field, irreducibility, reducedness, characteristic, completeness or local-ring hypothesis is imposed.
proofSteps: Write g=a·f+b with b∈v^(n+1) using native principal-ideal sum membership. Since g and b lie in v^n, f·a lies in v^n.
Use the exact-order ideal preimage to obtain a∈v^(n−d), with d+(n−d)=n justified by d≤n. Select the native homogeneous component w=HC_(n−d)(a).
Apply native component multiplicativity at the two order lower bounds, and kill HC_n(b) by the next-power adapter. This proves the forward implication even when a=0.
Conversely homogeneity puts w in v^(n−d). Hence f·w∈v^n, and native component multiplicativity identifies its degree-n component with HC_d(f)·w.
The assumed component equality makes HC_n(g−f·w)=0. The next-power adapter yields g−f·w∈v^(n+1), supplying an actual witness of principal-ideal sum membership.
